title: The Model-Building Approach, Linear/Quadratic Delta-Gamma VaR, EWMA, GARCH(1,1), Kupiec Backtesting, and LTCM
prerequisites: Probability, multivariate normal distributions, and covariance matrices
Option Greeks (Delta and Gamma) and Taylor series expansions
Value at Risk (VaR) definition and historical simulation foundations
learningOutcomes: Calculate parametric portfolio risk using the model-building (variance-covariance) approach and evaluate diversification benefits ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-05]).
Differentiate linear delta approximation from quadratic delta-gamma pricing for option portfolios ([fact-03], [fact-04]).
Update daily volatility and capture volatility clustering using EWMA and GARCH(1,1) models ([fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
Validate VaR model accuracy using Kupiec's Proportion of Failures (POF) backtesting and analyze LTCM failure causes ([fact-09], [fact-10], [fact-11]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Linear delta approximations completely ignore non-linear option curvature (Gamma), leading to severe risk miscalculations when underlying asset prices jump significantly ([fact-03], [fact-04]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Standard historical simulation weights past scenarios equally over a fixed window (e.g., 500 days), whereas model-building approaches use EWMA or GARCH to update volatility dynamically ([fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-11]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: As demonstrated by LTCM in 1998, historical correlations frequently jump toward 1.0 during panics, eliminating anticipated portfolio diversification benefits and breaking normal distribution VaR models ([fact-10]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A portfolio contains $10,000,000 in Microsoft shares (daily vol 2%) and $5,000,000 in AT&T shares (daily vol 1%) with correlation 0.3. Individual 99% VaRs are $465,200 for Microsoft and $116,300 for AT&T (sum = $581,500). Total portfolio 99% VaR is $496,600.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What is the exact diversification benefit achieved by combining Microsoft and AT&T? 2) How does EWMA update variance over time?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: The model-building approach calculates parametric portfolio risk using multivariate normal distributions and covariance matrices ([fact-01]).
Linear delta models must be upgraded to quadratic delta-gamma formulations to capture option curvature ([fact-03], [fact-04]).
EWMA and GARCH(1,1) models dynamically update variance and capture volatility clustering, while model failures at LTCM highlight correlation breakdown risks ([fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-10]).
